Minimal detail, clean form (e.g. Easy to reproduce and recognise quickly)
Distinctive and easy to recall (e.g. Brand recognition without context)
Avoids short-lived trends (e.g. Longevity saves redesign costs)
Works at any size and medium (e.g. Consistency across print, digital, merch)
Reflects brand values and audience (e.g. Correct message to correct people)

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: A good logo just needs to look great on a screen. Correct: A logo must work across ALL applications — business card, website, signage, uniform, packaging, social media. It must be legible at tiny sizes and reproduced in colour AND black-and-white. Test your logo at multiple scales.

Create a complete brand identity for a fictional company. Design the logo, choose colours and typography, and apply the identity across at least three different media. Include brand guidelines documentation.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Branding and Corporate Identity
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Branding and Corporate Identity using appropriate art vocabulary. Identify techniques, materials and processes accurately.

Corporate identity is the visual representation of a brand — the consistent use of logo, colours, typography, imagery and tone of voice across all communications. It distinguishes a company from competitors and builds recognition. A brand style guide (or brand manual) documents these elements to ensure consistency across all media. Strong corporate identity builds trust and makes a brand instantly

Effective logos follow five principles: Simple (easy to recognise and reproduce), Memorable (distinctive and easy to recall), Timeless (avoids trends that date quickly), Versatile (works at any size and in any medium), and Appropriate (reflects the brand's values and audience). A good logo works in full colour, single colour, reversed (white on dark), and at very small sizes.
